title: The Fed only reads two numbers
hook: The world economy is huge. How can two numbers run the whole thing?
metaphor: The Fed is a thermostat with two readings: how fast prices rise, and how many people have jobs. Too hot, turn it down. Too cold, turn it up.
body: Job one is keeping prices from rising too fast.
Job two is keeping as many people employed as possible.
Raising rates cools prices but costs jobs. Lowering rates does the opposite.
Almost every big money move starts with this one trade-off.

live.template: Prices are running about {pce}% a year against a {target}% goal, and unemployment is about {unrate}%.

caveat: The Fed watches far more than two numbers. These two just explain most of what it does.
